summary: Describes a Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace for the Internet2 Middleware Architecture Committee for Education (MACE). The namespace is for naming persistent resources defined by MACE, its working groups and other designated subordinates. It is a registration document for the namespace, not a new protocol.

eli5.summary: A school gives every student an ID number that never changes, even if the student moves. This document sets up a naming system like that, so one education group can give its things permanent names.

questions: how does mace assign persistent names
subtitle: A permanent naming system for education-related resources and standards.

tldr.problem: Educational institutions and organizations need to give persistent, permanent names to the documents, schemas, and standards they create, so resources can be reliably identified even if they move or servers change.
tldr.mechanism: A URN namespace named urn:mace is registered, using a hierarchical structure where each level is a colon-separated token. MACE (the Middleware Architecture Committee for Education) manages the top level and delegates branches to working groups and institutions.
tldr.outcome: Organizations in the higher education community can assign and resolve globally unique, persistent names to their resources without central coordination.

today: RFC 3613 is Informational and remains the formal URN namespace registration for MACE. The namespace is maintained by the Internet2 MACE community for naming persistent resources in higher education and related organizations.

sections.title: Why MACE Needs Persistent Names
sections.content:
The Internet2 Middleware Architecture Committee for Education (MACE) creates specifications, working drafts, XML schemas, stylesheets, and controlled vocabularies used by the higher education community. As these resources evolve and change locations, organizations need permanent names that point to them reliably.

A Uniform Resource Name (URN) is a type of Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) designed for exactly this purpose. Unlike a URL, which changes when a resource moves, a URN remains the same and is resolved through an infrastructure independent of any single web server. This document registers a formal URN namespace for MACE called mace.
sections.eli5: MACE makes documents for schools. Instead of a web address that breaks when the server moves, MACE gives each document a permanent name that always works.

sections.title: How MACE URN Names Are Structured
sections.content:
All MACE URNs follow the form urn:mace:colon:delimited:tokens. The tokens form a hierarchy, left to right, from highest authority to the specific resource. The syntax allows letters, digits, and special characters like hyphens, dots, and underscores, with colons used only to separate tokens.

For example, a working group might create names under urn:mace:shibboleth, and an institution might use urn:mace:georgetown.edu based on its domain name. The namespace specification conforms fully to RFC 2141 (URN Syntax), ensuring compatibility with URN resolution infrastructure.

Naming authorities at each level are responsible for ensuring uniqueness of names at their level and delegating authority downward. MACE directors maintain an index of all registered URNs on a web site for discovery and validation.
sections.eli5: Names are like file paths: urn:mace:school:department:document. Each level is managed by the people below it, so everyone gets a unique name.

sections.title: Assignment and Persistence
sections.content:
MACE directors create an initial set of immediate subordinate naming authorities and define a process for adding more. Each MACE working group designates a naming authority and proposes candidate names. Institutions can request subordinate authority status by contacting MACE through their institutional liaison.

To guarantee persistence, MACE directors contact each naming authority at least annually. If there is no response or the authority wishes to relinquish control, that branch reverts to MACE for reassignment. This process prevents orphaned branches of the namespace and ensures that responsibility for any branch lapses for less than a year.

Names are assigned case-insensitively at the top level (so two authorities will not differ only in case), and assigned names are treated as case-sensitive for all other purposes.
sections.eli5: MACE keeps a phone tree and calls once a year. If someone moves or quits, MACE takes that branch back and finds someone new.

sections.title: Resolution and Validation
sections.content:
Resolution of a MACE URN is the process of finding what resource or resource specification the URN points to. MACE maintains a central index on its web site mapping all MACE and workgroup-assigned URNs to resource identifiers or specifications. MACE-affiliated naming authorities specify how to resolve the URNs they assign.

Validation means confirming that a URN is legitimate. Presence in the MACE index implies validity. Subordinate authorities specify their own validation mechanisms. This two-level approach allows MACE to govern the overall namespace while delegating specifics to working groups and institutions.
sections.eli5: MACE keeps a directory of all names and what they point to. When someone asks 'is this a real MACE name?', MACE checks the directory.

sections.title: Scope and Considerations
sections.content:
The MACE namespace is global in scope and can assign URNs to very fine-grained objects, such as specific values in controlled vocabularies or individual XML elements. This makes it more suitable for MACE needs than broader namespaces like XMLORG, which are intended for different purposes.

MACE chose its own namespace rather than becoming a subordinate of an existing namespace because it seeks naming autonomy and wants to avoid fixed prefixes on every URN. MACE also names non-XML objects, which further justified having its own namespace.
sections.eli5: MACE can name small things (like one field in a form) or big things (like a whole standard). It doesn't have to ask permission from other organizations.
